EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong and moist trough pushed inland during the middle portion of February, leading to several days of impactful weather. On 2/18/26 in particular, the combination of precipitating snow and winds with blowing snow resulted in periods of very limited visibility and roadway hazards.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Wyoming Highway Patrol in addition to other law enforcement and first responders reported that a multi-vehicle accident occurred on I-80 near Evanston at mile marker 18 at approximately 3:00 PM 2/18/26. The crashes are said to have happened more or less simultaneously, involving 32 vehicles (20 semi trucks, 12 passenger vehicles), which blocked and closed both the westbound and eastbound lanes. The interstate was closed from mile marker 6 to mile marker 34, lasting from roughly 3:28 PM  until 4:00 AM the following morning. As a result of the collisions, 2 fatalities were confirmed, as were 22 injuries, 3 of which required helicopter transportation to Utah emergency facilities. Additionally, a tractor trailer carrying livestock suffered severe enough impact to kill 6 of the cattle inside. Around the time of the pileup a nearby mesonet sensor was observing conditions including gusts in excess of 30 mph and visibility around one quarter of a mile, likely due to blowing snow. Wyoming Highway Patrol suspects excessive speed for the ongoing poor winter weather conditions to be a likely cause.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very strong ridge of high pressure set up across much of the western United States and brought an long period of record breaking warmth. The most impressive stretch was from March 18 through March 21. In total, 71 new daily record high temperatures were set out of a possible 126 high temperatures at RIW CLI sites (longer term climate sites), greater than half of the daily highs. Every location was at least 10 degrees above normal through the period. Every location had their all time warmest period for these two weeks, with three locations; the Riverton Airport, the Sweetwater County airport near Rock Springs, and the Lander airport; more than 8 degrees above the previous warmest period. All locations set their all time high temperature March multiple times in this stretch. Six locations had their earliest 80 degree high temperature, with four stations having their first 80 degree or greater March high temperatures in station history.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: It was a record warm period for much of the latter half of March. The period averaged nearly 15 degrees above normal, with every day but one at least 10 degrees above normal for the daily average temperature. Ten of these days set daily record high temperatures. The previous all time monthly high temperature of 69 was tied or broken six times. This includes four high temperatures in the 70s, which are the first four occurrences on 70 degree temperatures in station history, including the new monthly record high of 73. Records at the Big Piney airport date back to 1998.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An area of low pressure moved across the area and brought heavy snow, especially to the  mountains. The heaviest snow fell in the Tetons, where there were many reports of over a foot of new snow with a maximum amount of 25 inches at the top of the Jackson Hole Ski Resort. Other notable amounts included 20 inches in the Salt and Wyoming Range, 15 inches in the Bighorn Range, 14 inches in the western Wind River Range and 12 inches on Casper Mountain. Lesser amounts fell in the lower elevations. However, in northern Johnson County, a combination of snow and wind gusting to 50 mph brought closures of Interstates 25 and 90 for a time.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A combination of snow and wind gusting over 50 mph brought very difficult travel to northern Johnson County, including the closure of Interstates 25 and 90.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A grazing shortwave trough north of Utah sent a cold front into the region. Ahead of and along this boundary there was enough moisture to result in isolated to scattered convective development, with much of this activity higher based in nature. As a result, several strong to severe wind gusts were recorded or reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Evanston North mesonet station recorded an initial wind gust of 58 mph, followed by a peak wind gust of 59 mph, as a result of outflow winds associated with a nearby cluster of convective showers and thunderstorms moving through the area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An area of low pressure passed to the south of Wyoming and brought snow to central and southern portions of the state. The heaviest amounts of snow fell in the favored northeast upslope areas. Some notable amounts in the mountains included 23 inches on Casper Mountain and 19 inches above Sinks Canyon Park near Lander. In the lower elevations, 8 inches of new snow fell in Casper and Jeffrey City and 5 to 12 inches fell near Lander. In Eastern Sweetwater County, the Green Mountains and Wind River Range, winds gusting as over 55 mph brought local blizzard conditions, leading to closure of Interstate 80, US 287 and South Pass during the storm.
